# Vishal Akshintala

> Registered Advocate practicing litigation and corporate advisory in AI governance, data privacy, cybersecurity law, and space law, across India, the EU, UK, US, and APAC. Court representation across Telangana and pan-India on referral. NALSAR University of Law alumnus, ISO/IEC 42001 Lead Implementer, CIPP/E and AIGP (IAPP), affiliated with Radhical Global Attorneys (Hyderabad, India).

Vishal Akshintala represents clients in litigation before Telangana courts and regulatory forums — including cybercrime matters (both complainants and accused), bail and anticipatory bail in cyber cases, bank account freezes in cybercrime investigations, police notices to appear, data protection grievances, and commercial/TDSAT disputes — and separately advises organizations on AI risk classification under the EU AI Act, data fiduciary obligations under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) 2023, cybersecurity incident-response obligations under CERT-In directions, and jurisdictional questions in space law including orbital data infrastructure and satellite AI systems under the 1967 Outer Space Treaty. He also delivers one-on-one and cohort AI governance training programs for legal and compliance teams.

- [Legal Help](https://vishalakshintala.in/legal-help.html): direct query submission, available in English, Hindi, and Telugu
- [Insights](https://vishalakshintala.in/insights.html): long-form legal commentary, including a public interest litigation argument on FIR data disclosure and analysis of digital arrest scams
- [Bank account frozen in a cybercrime investigation](https://vishalakshintala.in/bank-account-frozen.html): what a freeze is, what the law says about seizure and release, first steps, and how to send a query
- [Bail and police notices in cyber cases](https://vishalakshintala.in/cyber-bail-police-notice.html): notice to appear, rights on arrest, bail and anticipatory bail under the BNSS, in plain words
- [DPDP Act compliance for companies](https://vishalakshintala.in/dpdp-compliance.html): the dates in the DPDP Rules, 2025, what they ask for, and how the compliance work is done
- [AI governance for companies](https://vishalakshintala.in/ai-governance.html): EU AI Act dates and risk tiers, ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF, impact assessments and audits

## Articles

- [GM $220m multistate settlement — driving data sold on to insurers](https://vishalakshintala.in/insight-gm-driver-data-settlement.html): How often you drove, when, how hard you braked, whether you sped. 36 US attorneys general say General Motors sold that on.
- [EDPB anonymisation — three tests](https://vishalakshintala.in/insight-edpb-anonymisation-three-tests.html): Deleting the names column does not make a dataset anonymous. The European Data Protection Board has set out three tests that it should pass.
- [CNIL fines Fnac €7m — app tracker without consent](https://vishalakshintala.in/insight-cnil-fnac-app-tracker.html): You browsed a shopping app. A tracker inside it reported what you looked at, without your consent.
- [Canada's privacy regulators on AI in health](https://vishalakshintala.in/insight-canada-health-ai-resolution.html): If you build AI for healthcare, Canada's privacy regulators have set out what they expect from you and from the hospitals that buy from you.
- [California AG settles with Lyft — opt-out outside the app](https://vishalakshintala.in/insight-california-lyft-opt-out.html): Logged in, using the app, and asked to log in again before you could say no to the sale of your data.
- [OAIC breach statistics Jan–Jun 2026](https://vishalakshintala.in/insight-oaic-breach-statistics-h1-2026.html): Australia's breach numbers barely moved in six months. The size of the breaches did.
- [ICO reprimands — Password1 test account](https://vishalakshintala.in/insight-ico-password1-reprimand.html): One forgotten test account, one weak password, and the data of 3,300 people, most of them children.
- [EN 18286 — first EU AI Act harmonised standard](https://vishalakshintala.in/insight-en-18286-ai-act-qms-standard.html): The EU AI Act now has its first harmonised standard, and it is about quality management.
